judged_text: A Salesforce token refresh is now executed unconditionally on every service instantiation — not routed through refreshOAuthTokens like the other eight apps — and success is detected via `response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is empty under HTTP/2 or reason-phrase-stripping proxies. Every calendar operation pays an extra Salesforce round-trip even when the stored token is valid; behind an HTTP/2 proxy the check throws 400 on successful responses; and in sync mode the refresh bypasses the sync endpoint, diverging from the protocol the rest of this PR implements.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token fetch to Salesforce (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)`) immediately after reading `credential.key`, before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no gating on token expiry and it is not routed through the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper used elsewhere in this PR, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will still hit Salesforce directly (diverging from the new sync mode protocol). Additionally, success is checked via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`, which is less reliable than `response.ok`/`response.status` and can be empty depending on the fetch/HTTP stack; this can incorrectly throw on otherwise-successful responses.
